blind_target.authors: Roter, D. L., Hall, J. A., Katz, N. R.
blind_target.title: Relations between physicians’ behaviors and analogue patients’ satisfaction, recall and impressions
blind_target.evidence_quote:
In the last of her two papers about the
relative relevance of instrumental or task-re-
lated behavior on one hand, and socio-emo-
tional or affective behavior on the other,
Roter called on other researchers “‘to repli-
cate her findings through different method-
ologies and in the natural setting.’”* This call
was based on two possible weaknesses of
her study: 1) the use of simulated patients
instead of real patients, which raises ques-
tions about the generalization of the results,
and 2) the use of audiotapes instead of video-
tapes, which limited the possibility to regis-
ter nonverbal affect to vocal-tone, only. Our
study can be seen as such a replication: it
took place in the natural setting (real general
practitioners with real patients who had hy-
pertension) and used partly different meth-
odologies (video instead of audio, which
made it possible to register visual as well vo-
cal cues). In addition, some refinements
have been made in RIAS to get a more de-
tailed picture of GP’s socio-emotional behav-
ior.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
The results presented partly corroborate
those from the previous studies in which
Roter’s Interaction Analysis System was
used, but they also shed some new light on
the controversies found in the literature
about the relative relevance of instrumental
versus affective behavior.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Discussion explicitly describes partial corroboration of the earlier RIAS studies, then identifies both shared associations and important differences, including failure to corroborate the overall primacy of task-related behavior.

prior_decision.reason: The paper explicitly frames itself as a replication responding to the call in the second of the two 1987 companion papers (Reference 8, Roter, Hall, & Katz, 1987) and repeatedly compares its findings against both papers jointly, making Reference 8 a valid omitted target with a mixed outcome.

luna_triage.reason: The paper explicitly calls its natural-setting study a replication of the second 1987 Roter, Hall, and Katz paper and compares results against it. The supplied row 649 is the distinct companion article by Hall, Roter, and Katz, 'Task versus socio-emotional behaviors in physicians'; publication-level deduplication does not merge the two different papers.
luna_triage.omission_quote: Our study can be seen as such a replication: it took place in the natural setting (real general practitioners with real patients who had hypertension) and used partly different methodologies (video instead of audio, which made it possible to register visual as well vocal cues).

unresolved_objection: Different companion publication alone is not proof of genuinely missing original work/finding. Hall/Roter/Katz1987 and Roter/Hall/Katz1987 may share analogue-patient data, different analyses or independent empirical findings. Resolve actual same-study/report equivalence AND which finding Bensing retests. Distinguish an alternate report of a represented original from an empirically distinct original finding, consistent with codebook paper-level pairing. Sharing data alone also does not prove same finding. Do not infer either way from DOI inequality. Read prior positive, review0004 and both supplied primary abstracts. If evidence cannot settle, use undeterminable.
